vendors.description: Axon Enterprise body-worn camera line (Body 2, Body 3, Body 4). Widely deployed by US law enforcement. Identified via OUI blocks, BLE manufacturer ID 0x034D, BLE service UUID 0xFFA1 (per operator captures), officer-assignment SSID pattern X_[initial][surname], and Bluetooth CoD 0x1F00 (per operator captures).
vendors.confidence_notes: OUI blocks sourced from IEEE registry; consistent with FCC filing data. BLE mfgrid 0x034D and service UUID 0xFFA1 confirmed from captured devices. CoD 0x1F00 confirmed across 23 observed Axon units per operator dataset.

vendors.confidence_notes: BLE mfgrid 0x034D shared with Axon BWC. Classification as SIGNAL vs BWC depends on BLE advertisement name pattern.

vendors.description: Flock Safety fixed automated license plate recognition (ALPR) cameras. Deployed by municipal police, county sheriffs, HOAs, and private entities across the US. Each camera broadcasts a WiFi network for management and cellular upload. Identified via proprietary OUI blocks, canonical SSID pattern Flock-[6 hex chars], and BLE manufacturer ID 0x09C8 (XUNTONG).
vendors.confidence_notes: 23 HIGH-confidence OUI prefixes listed here; additional medium-confidence contract-manufacturer OUIs seeded in DB migrations (see 20260531_031). SSID Flock-[hex6] is EXACT match per operator captures. BLE mfgrid 0x09C8 shared with FS_EXT_BATTERY and RAVEN_GUNSHOT_DETECTOR; disambiguate via BLE name.

docs.title: Flock Safety License Plate Readers — Product Page
docs.summary: Official Flock Safety LPR product page. Confirms solar-powered, LTE-connected cameras with WiFi management interface. Covers Vehicle Signature technology, NightVision, NCIC integration, 5,000+ law enforcement agencies, and National LPR Network with billions of monthly plate reads. Data retention: 30-day default, up to 1 year.

vendors.description: Flock Safety external battery / solar power unit paired with ALPR cameras in locations without grid power. Broadcasts its own WiFi management interface. Identified via a subset of Flock OUI blocks and BLE name prefix 'fs ext battery'.
vendors.confidence_notes: OUI subset of Flock Safety allocations. Upserting FS_EXT_BATTERY after FLOCK_SAFETY_CAMERA in DB ensures battery OUIs carry correct sub-type.

docs.title: Flock Safety License Plate Readers — Product Page
docs.summary: Official Flock Safety LPR product page. Documents solar-powered battery deployment model for off-grid camera locations. Confirms shared Flock product ecosystem including external battery units.

vendors.description: ShotSpotter (now SoundThinking) acoustic gunshot detection sensors mounted on utility poles and rooftops. Deployed in 180+ US cities per manufacturer (2026). Each sensor node maintains a WiFi management interface. Uses acoustic triangulation requiring 3+ sensors to hear same sound. 97% accuracy per manufacturer (2019-2021 reported data). Identified via OUI D4:11:D6 and SSID patterns matching SoundThinking, ShotSpotter, SST-, SENSOR-, SNS-, or acoustic prefixes.
vendors.confidence_notes: OUI D4:11:D6 confirmed from captured devices. SSID pattern is MEDIUM confidence alone; combined with OUI is HIGH.

docs.title: SoundThinking ShotSpotter — Gunshot Detection System Product Page
docs.summary: Official SoundThinking ShotSpotter product page. Covers acoustic sensor array architecture, triangulation method, 60-second detection-to-alert time, 97% accuracy (manufacturer-reported), 24x7 Incident Review Center, privacy protections (NYU Policing Project audit), SOC2 compliance, and platform integrations (CAD/RMS, LPR, drones, RTCC). OUI D4:11:D6 associated with SoundThinking hardware per operator observations.

vendors.description: Raven Alert gunshot detection platform by Flock Safety. Acoustic sensor nodes using BLE for local communication. Detects gunshots, sideshows, crashes, and fireworks via event-triggered acoustic recognition. Not always-on recording; activates only on acoustic signatures of interest. Integrates with Flock LPR and video via FlockOS. Identified via BLE manufacturer ID 0x09C8 (XUNTONG, shared Flock Safety component supplier) and BLE device name prefix 'raven'.
vendors.confidence_notes: BLE mfgrid 0x09C8 shared across Flock Safety product family. BLE name ^raven disambiguates from FLOCK_SAFETY_CAMERA and FS_EXT_BATTERY.

docs.title: Flock Safety Gunshot and Audio Detection — Product Page
docs.summary: Official Flock Safety audio/gunshot detection product page. Covers event-triggered acoustic detection (gunshots, sideshows, crashes, fireworks), BLE-based sensor communication, FlockOS integration with LPR and video, policy-governed activation (not always-on), tamper detection, and RTCC workflow design. Confirms Raven branding under Flock Safety audio detection umbrella.

vendors.description: Unknown-vendor body-worn camera advertising under the DEI-[serial] BLE name pattern. All observed units use randomized MACs, CoD 0x1F00 (consistent with deliberate obfuscation), and a proprietary BLE service UUID b4520100-a308-4e56-8a52-536c2ad07147. Vendor attribution unconfirmed; possible candidates include Digital Ally (FirstVu line).
vendors.confidence_notes: SSID pattern DEI-[0-9]+ is STRONG. Service UUID b4520100-… confirmed exclusive to DEI- devices in operator dataset; EXACT confidence when present.

vendors.description: Generic Bluetooth device self-identifying as an imaging camera via Bluetooth Class of Device (CoD) major class 0x06 (Imaging), minor 0x20 (Camera). Encompasses dashcams, security cameras, and non-Axon body-worn cameras from various vendors.
vendors.confidence_notes: CoD is self-reported and could be spoofed. MEDIUM confidence alone; meaningful when corroborated with location or behavioral data.

vendors.confidence_notes: OUI blocks cover commercial and enterprise product lines; not exclusive to public safety. SSID corroboration increases confidence. Not yet in active detection vocab — library-only entry for Phase 1.

vendors.description: Hak5 WiFi Pineapple Mark VII and Enterprise series. Dual-use pentest / RF auditing platform that performs rogue AP attacks, PineAP beacon-response injection, and passive WiFi reconnaissance. Mark VII: 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n (5 GHz/ac with module), single-core MIPS, 3 radios, 256MB RAM, 2GB eMMC, USB-C. Enterprise: 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac wave2, quad-core ARM, 4 radios, 1GB RAM. Widely used in authorized penetration tests.
vendors.confidence_notes: No fixed OUI — SoC OUI varies by hardware revision (MIPS or ARM vendor). Detection via default SSID 'pineapple' or characteristic management interface patterns. High FP risk; correlate with behavioral data before flagging. FCC ID 2A4RG-MARK7 (reported — unverified; no FCC filing archived). Not yet in active detection vocab — library-only entry for Phase 1.

docs.title: Hak5 WiFi Pineapple — Mark VII & Enterprise Shop Page
docs.summary: Official Hak5 shop product page for WiFi Pineapple Mark VII and Enterprise. Mark VII specs: 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n (5 GHz/ac with module), single-core MIPS SoC, 3 dedicated role-based radios, 256MB RAM, 2GB eMMC, USB-C power. Enterprise specs: 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac wave2, quad-core ARM, 4 radios, 1GB RAM, 4GB eMMC, AC power. Features PineAP suite, WPA Enterprise capture, passive surveillance, cloud C2.

vendors.description: Flipper Zero multi-tool RF / hardware hacking device by Flipper Devices Inc. MCU: STM32WB55RG (ARM Cortex-M4 64MHz + M0+ 32MHz). Sub-1GHz via CC1101 (315/433/868/915MHz), NFC 13.56MHz, 125kHz RFID, IR transceiver, iButton 1-Wire, BLE 5.4, GPIO. Battery: LiPo 2100mAh, 28-day life. Fully open-source firmware (github.com/flipperdevices/flipperzero-firmware). BLE default device name 'Flipper Zero'; BLE service UUIDs publicly documented.
vendors.confidence_notes: BLE device name 'Flipper Zero' is distinctive and unlikely to appear on production consumer hardware. BLE service UUIDs published in open-source firmware. No WiFi radio; not visible in wardriving captures. FCC ID 2A2PY-FLIPPER (reported — unverified; no FCC filing archived). Not yet in active detection vocab — library-only entry for Phase 1.

docs.title: Flipper Zero — Official Product Page and Full Technical Specifications
docs.summary: Official Flipper Zero product page with complete hardware specifications. MCU: STM32WB55RG (ARM Cortex-M4 64MHz + ARM Cortex-M0+ 32MHz). Sub-1GHz: CC1101 chip, 315/433/868/915MHz bands, up to 50m range. BLE 5.4: 4dBm TX, -96dBm RX. NFC 13.56MHz (MIFARE, DESFire, FeliCa, iClass). 125kHz RFID (EM410x, HID, Indala, etc.). IR transceiver. iButton 1-Wire. USB-C. GPIO 13 pins. LCD 128x64. LiPo 2100mAh.

vendors.description: Great Scott Gadgets Ubertooth One. Open-source Bluetooth monitoring and development platform. USB dongle used for passive BLE/BT sniffing and research. Latest release 2020-12-R1. Capable BLE sniffer and partial BR Bluetooth Classic sniffer. Produces no wireless emissions visible in standard wardriving captures; documented here for analyst reference.
vendors.confidence_notes: No WiFi or active BLE advertisement. Library-only entry — not detection-worthy from wardriving data.

docs.title: Ubertooth One — GitHub README (Great Scott Gadgets)
docs.summary: Official GitHub README for Project Ubertooth. Confirms open-source BT/BLE passive sniffer platform, USB dongle form factor, latest release 2020-12-R1, documentation at ubertooth.readthedocs.io. Capable of BLE sniffing and partial BR Bluetooth Classic sniffing. No active wireless emissions; not detectable from wardriving captures.

vendors.description: Proxmark3 RFID / NFC research and auditing tool. USB-connected hardware for reading, cloning, and emulating RFID/NFC credentials. Supports 125kHz LF (EM410x, HID, Indala, T5577) and 13.56MHz HF (MIFARE, DESFire, iClass, FeliCa, EMV). RDV4 hardware adds smart card module, FPC Bluetooth/battery addon. Iceman fork (RfidResearchGroup/proxmark3) is canonical community fork (5.7k stars). GPLv3.
vendors.confidence_notes: No WiFi or BLE emissions from base hardware. Blue Shark Bluetooth addon may produce a BLE advertisement. Library-only entry.

docs.title: Proxmark3 Iceman Fork — GitHub README
docs.summary: Official GitHub README for Proxmark3 Iceman fork (RfidResearchGroup/proxmark3). Covers supported RFID protocols (125kHz LF, 134kHz LF, 13.56MHz HF/NFC, EMV, CIPURSE), hardware variants (RDV4 flagship, RDV1/2/3, SE with BLE, Proxmark3 X), platform support (Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS), and GPLv3 license.

vendors.description: OUI block registered as private or to an unknown entity. Private OUI registrations are used by organizations that do not want their hardware publicly attributed. Presence alone does not indicate surveillance activity; requires corroboration from SSID, behavioral, or geospatial data.
vendors.confidence_notes: Classification is based solely on private OUI registration status. Treat as an anomaly indicator requiring analyst review rather than a confirmed surveillance device.
